claim: In the signal box we made an enterable building's front read as two storey bands (brick plinth, timber upper) from a lane with a lip 128 deep along its face, its floor at the plinth top and the lane's own sky. The lane's lower step draws the plinth in the lane's record, the lip's back wall the upper storey in the lip's. A lower sky on the lip would be refused by open-neighbours-share-a-sky unless out of a body's reach, so the lane's sky comes down to the roof line instead. Over a door the lane's upper band must be painted the upper storey's tile.
evidence: projects/signal-box/level/build.py:56-65 (OUTDOOR sky at TOP, BASE, LIP 128), :118-136 lip() and its connections, :196-197 the wall over the door painted BOARDS
use: For a two-band front seen from a street: a lip sector a few units deep, floor at the plinth top, under the street's sky; paint the street's wall above any door in the upper storey's tile.
